article_title: Bridging the gaps in problem-based learning: an evidence-based intervention in bachelor of medicine and surgery (MBBS) program.
citation: Ullah Himayat, Huma Sarwat, Naeem Lubna, Yunus Mohammed, Sarfraz Junaid. (2025). Bridging the gaps in problem-based learning: an evidence-based intervention in bachelor of medicine and surgery (MBBS) program. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07003-2
title: The Hung 3C3R PBL problem design model
description: The 3C3R model is a systematic approach for designing effective PBL problems, which the article adopted to revise its problem bank. The article describes it as having "two components: core components and processing components". Core components (3C) — content, context, and connections — promote content/concept learning, while processing components (3R) — researching, reasoning, and reflecting — target learners' cognitive learning processes and problem-solving abilities. The article credits it with enhancing PBL qualities and resolving implementation challenges identified in prior PBL research.
requirements: Problems designed so core components (content, context, connections) align with intended learning objectives
constraints: The article applies it specifically to PBL problem design in medical education
target_learning_goals: Problem design that supports content/concept learning and problem-solving abilities
examples: Used by the PBL revision committee to revise 136 PBL problems across 12 blocks
